title: Empowering informal caregivers of people with dementia through an adapted and expanded version of the WHO e-health intervention iSupport - a randomized study
summary:
Demographic change and population ageing in Germany are associated with an increasing number of people living with dementia. Most of these individuals live at home and depend on support from informal caregivers, usually family members. Providing care can place a considerable burden on relatives; at the same time, lack of time and limited mobility often make it difficult to access existing support services. Therefore, easily accessible support services are needed that demonstrably reduce caregivers’ burden and strengthen their ability to manage the caregiving situation.

iSupport Germany is a digital learning and support platform for informal caregivers of people with dementia. It is based on the iSupport programme developed by the World Health Organization (WHO). The programme has been adapted and expanded for the German healthcare context and provides information and support for everyday caregiving.

This study investigates whether iSupport Germany can reduce the burden experienced by informal caregivers. For this purpose, two groups will be compared: one group will receive immediate access to iSupport Germany, while the other group will be placed on a waiting list and will receive access only after completion of the assessments at 3 months.
conditions: Caregiver burden of informal caregivers of people with dementia

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Informal caregiver of a person with dementia
- Adequate proficiency in German
Exclusion criteria:
- Suicidal ideation
- The person with dementia resides in a long-term care facility
